title: Define the provisioning session as a delivered engagement
description:
**Phase 1 of 5.**

- **Blocked by:** the hand-provisioning task
- **Runs in parallel with:** the rest of this epic
- **Unblocks:** the setup fee tiers, in the paid enablement epic

---
A chore because the deliverable is an agreed way of working, not code.

Bring-your-own-AWS means no customer reaches a running organization without a person from Anthus in a call with them. That is not a support ticket to be minimized. It is a 60-to-90 minute session with a named engineer that ends with their first team of bots configured and running — and it is the highest-signal customer research available at any price, with a decision-maker in the room at the moment they are most invested.

**Professional services stops being an upsell here and becomes the main motion.** Every onboarding is already a small consulting engagement; the only question is whether it is run deliberately.

Define: who runs it, what the agenda is, what gets recorded afterwards, and what the handoff into a scoping conversation looks like for the ones who want more.

Keep the in-product counterpart restrained by contrast — one quiet line in organization settings is enough. The session is the pitch.

**Done when:** the session agenda and the post-session record template are in the wiki, and the first one has been run against a real customer.
